skill.name: amazon-buy-box-monitor-api-skill
skill.description: Extract Amazon buy box, pricing, seller, fulfillment, and availability details for a supplied ASIN using the BrowserAct API workflow.
skill.summary: Monitor Amazon buy box and seller data through a BrowserAct API workflow.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill performs intended outbound BrowserAct API calls and handles a BrowserAct API key. Most Markdown backtick and reconnaissance detections are false positives, but credential collection guidance, bearer-token handling, external command execution, and unvalidated marketplace URLs remain real review concerns.

remediation.issue: The instructions allow users to provide BROWSERACT_API_KEY to the agent.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to set BROWSERACT_API_KEY in their local environment or secret manager, and remove language that asks users to paste the key into chat.

remediation.issue: marketplace_url is accepted from the command line without validation.
remediation.suggestion: Validate the URL scheme and host against an allowlist of supported Amazon marketplace domains before starting the BrowserAct workflow.

remediation.issue: The skill executes a local Python script that makes third-party API requests.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact BrowserAct endpoints used, the data sent, and expected runtime before execution so users can give informed consent.

remediation.issue: The documentation markets avoidance of CAPTCHA, IP restrictions, and geo-fencing.
remediation.suggestion: Reword the feature list to emphasize compliant data access and remove claims about bypassing access controls.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe API Key Collection Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to prompt and wait for the user to provide BROWSERACT_API_KEY, and the script says the user may provide the key to the agent. This can expose a BrowserAct credential in chat transcripts or logs instead of keeping it in the environment.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The wording explicitly asks the agent to prompt for the missing key and tells the user they can provide it. This is direct evidence of credential collection guidance.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Marketplace URL Passed to Browser Automation
semantic_findings.description: The script accepts marketplace_url from the command line and passes it into the BrowserAct workflow without validating that it is an Amazon marketplace URL. A user or calling agent could direct the workflow to an unintended URL using the user's BrowserAct account.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly assigns sys.argv[2] to marketplace_url and passes it into the task runner. The downstream BrowserAct template behavior is not shown, so confidence is high enough to flag but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Anti-Bot Evasion Positioning
semantic_findings.description: The documentation advertises no CAPTCHA issues and no IP access restrictions or geo-fencing. This positions the skill as a way to avoid access controls around automated Amazon data collection.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The claims are explicit in the feature list and relate to avoiding common anti-automation protections. The text does not show exploit code, so this is a contextual marketplace risk.

content.value_statement: Amazon sellers need current buy box, price, and seller data. This skill runs a BrowserAct workflow to collect structured ASIN-level marketplace details.
actual_capabilities: Starts a BrowserAct workflow template for a supplied Amazon ASIN.
Accepts an optional Amazon marketplace URL for regional checks.
Polls BrowserAct task status with timestamped progress messages.
Returns product title, buy box owner, price, currency, and availability when available.
Reports other sellers, fulfillment method, seller rating, and feedback count when returned by the API.
Shows clear errors for missing keys, invalid authorization, failed tasks, and timeouts.
limitations: Requires a BrowserAct account and BROWSERACT_API_KEY.
Sends ASIN and marketplace parameters to BrowserAct for processing.
Depends on BrowserAct workflow availability and Amazon page behavior.
Does not validate marketplace URLs before sending them to the workflow.

best_practices: Store BROWSERACT_API_KEY in an environment variable or secret manager.
Use only supported Amazon marketplace URLs for the marketplace parameter.
Review BrowserAct and Amazon usage terms before automating repeated checks.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into shared chats, tickets, or logs.
Do not use non-Amazon URLs as marketplace inputs.
Do not treat the output as a guaranteed real-time alerting feed.

faq.question: What input does this skill need?
faq.answer: It needs an Amazon ASIN and can also accept a marketplace URL such as an Amazon regional domain.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires BROWSERACT_API_KEY for BrowserAct API access.

faq.question: What data can it return?
faq.answer: It can return buy box owner, price, currency, availability, fulfillment method, other sellers, ratings, and feedback count.

faq.question: Does it browse Amazon directly from my machine?
faq.answer: No. The script sends a workflow request to BrowserAct, which performs the configured automation.

faq.question: How long can a run take?
faq.answer: The script polls for up to five minutes and prints timestamped status messages while waiting.

faq.question: Can it monitor many ASINs continuously?
faq.answer: No. The provided script runs one ASIN per invocation and does not include scheduling or bulk monitoring.
